executive_assessment.text: Mali faces high and increasing climate pressure, but rainfall futures are substantially more uncertain than warming. Supporting evidence: MLI-E-001-004; pathways MLI-P-001-003. (World Bank)

The most credible Climate-FCV formulation is mediated and place-specific: livelihood and food-security stress, mobility, access governance and institutional performance can transmit climate pressure into FCV risk, while conflict and insecurity simultaneously erode adaptation and service delivery. Supporting evidence: MLI-E-005-020; pathways MLI-P-001-007. (Frontiers)

Mali possesses real resilience capacities - mobility, diversification, local institutions, formal climate-policy structures and community-driven programme mechanisms - but evaluated evidence shows that coping gains do not reliably translate into transformative productivity, durable stabilization or sustained outcomes. Supporting evidence: MLI-E-006, 009-010, 021-026; pathway MLI-P-008.

geographic_notes.text: *Northern and central Mali must not be treated as proxies for the whole country. SIPRI’s strongest security-pathway evidence emphasizes the north and centre, and the pastoral climate-risk survey evidence cited in that study is specifically from Gao and Mopti. (SIPRI)

*Ménaka, Gao, Mopti and Timbuktu currently show particularly acute combinations of insecurity, displacement/service strain and nutrition risk, but that does not imply identical drivers in each region. UNICEF projects especially severe lean-season nutritional stress in these areas. (UNICEF)

*The Inner Niger Delta is analytically distinct. Seasonal flooding supports rice, sorghum, pasture and fisheries, while pastoral movements into and out of the Delta make hydrological timing and access governance especially important. The retained evidence is sufficient to flag the distinct system but not to quantify current Delta-wide FCV effects. (SIPRI)

*Southern areas differ from conflict-affected northern/central zones. FAO reported generally favorable 2024 national cereal output despite localized flood losses and insecurity-related production shortfalls in northern and central regions, illustrating why national agricultural totals can obscure local crisis. (FAOHome)

*Urban evidence is comparatively thin. Bamako appears prominently in the 2026 service-access evidence because insecurity and blockade affected service continuity, but the retained evidence is much stronger on rural livelihoods than urban heat, drainage, informal settlements or climate-sensitive infrastructure. (United Nations Population Fund)

*Displaced, refugee and host populations require separate treatment. UNHCR’s portal reports refugee and IDP series from different administrative sources and update dates; they should not be merged into a single undifferentiated “displaced population” estimate. (UNHCR Data Portal)

sector_notes.text: *Strongest coverage: rain-fed agriculture, pastoralism/livestock, food security, humanitarian services, local/natural-resource governance and peacebuilding/stabilization.
*Moderate coverage: water access/irrigation, education, nutrition, health, mobility and community institutions.

*Thin coverage: fisheries despite Inner Niger Delta importance; urban climate systems; hydropower; detailed groundwater dynamics; private-sector adaptation; climate-sensitive transport; disability-specific vulnerability; rigorous gender-differentiated adaptation outcomes; and contemporary post-2023 evaluation of local adaptation/peace programmes.

known_gaps.text: Climate projections: warming is robust, but precipitation magnitude and direction remain uncertain. More subnational, bias-corrected projections are needed for rainfall intensity, drought duration, flood return periods and agro-pastoral seasonal timing. (World Bank)

Extreme-event attribution: retained sources support rising climate risk but do not justify attributing individual floods or drought losses to anthropogenic climate change without event-attribution evidence.

Geographic gaps: northern/central Mali is over-represented in Climate-FCV studies relative to southern rural zones and urban systems. Inner Niger Delta fisheries and current pastoral corridors require more recent evidence.

Population gaps: differentiated quantitative evidence remains limited for women, girls, persons with disabilities, older people, minority/ethnic groups and households with different displacement status. SIPRI supports differentiation but not a complete national profile. (SIPRI)

Causal uncertainty: the peer-reviewed SEM supports a food-security mediation pathway but is observational. The qualitative climate-security study is explicitly a single-case plausibility probe. Neither warrants a deterministic national climate-conflict claim. (Frontiers)

FCV-to-climate evidence: there is strong descriptive evidence that conflict disrupts markets, irrigation, mobility and service delivery, but few studies formally estimate how much these disruptions reduce household or institutional climate-adaptation performance.
Programme evaluation: the strongest independent synthesis ends in 2021. Newer climate-resilience, community-service and peace-supporting interventions have limited independent outcome evidence.

Unintended effects: the IOB review demonstrates that unintended peacebuilding incentives can occur, but there is little equivalent evaluation of whether adaptation projects alter land values, resource access, elite capture or intergroup relations.

Institutional implementation: a formal NDC coordination mechanism exists, but there is insufficient verified evidence here on execution rates, budget disbursement, regional coverage or adaptation outcomes under NDC 2.0. (Government of Mali)

NDC document access: the official UNFCCC PDF was retrievable, but its large size prevented browser rendering; the exact PDF page for the retained §6.2 adaptation list could not be confirmed through the browser and is therefore explicitly marked LOCATOR NOT VERIFIED. (UNFCCC)

Access bias in humanitarian evidence: insecurity restricts observation and delivery in precisely the locations likely to have high vulnerability; apparently “lower” needs in poorly accessed locations may reflect data limitations.

Current displacement-series comparability: UNHCR’s displayed refugee figures are updated later than its displayed IDP series. Analysts should use indicator-specific reference dates rather than implying a single June 2026 snapshot. (UNHCR Data Portal)
